All three variants share the same user content, shown last; {report} is replaced with the report body, truncated to 4000 characters. The system content differs by which section headers are present in the raw report.
Figure 2: Overall framework of UR2-MLLM, including (a) multimodal reasoning trajectory construction, (b) training pipeline overview, and (c) stage-wise training details.

Table 6: Dataset sizes used by UR2-MLLM. “Image-level” counts the unique image-report pairs that become training (or evaluation) samples; “item-level” counts the finer-grained annotations derived from each pair, since a single MIMIC-CXR study yields multiple bbox-uncertainty annotations during Stage 1 curation and a single ImaGenome-anchored sentence yields multiple revisit regions during Stage 2 curation, so item-level counts are strictly larger than image-level counts wherever applicable. Stage 3 uses MIMIC-CXR image-report pairs without additional annotation. IU-Xray is used only for out-of-domain evaluation; its “item-level” column counts the individual frontal and lateral DICOM images, since a single report covers both views.
Table 3: NLG metrics for radiology report generation on the IU X-ray dataset (Best, Second-best).

Figure 6: Frequency distribution of uncertainty markers in MIMIC-CXR ground-truth reports. All 276,778 reports (train+val+test) were scanned for occurrences of the 35-term closed vocabulary used during Stage 2 trace synthesis (longest-first masked matching, case-insensitive, whole-word boundary). Top three markers (likely, may, appears) cover 48.8% of all 155,542 mentions; the top ten cover 84%. Multi-word constructions (consistent with, concerning for, compatible with) appear prominently among the top seven.

Figure 7: Per-thousand-word frequency of the top fourteen uncertainty markers across four corpora. Bars within each group correspond, from left to right, to ground-truth MIMIC-CXR reports, the Stage 2 SFT model, the full-reward GRPO model, and the no-revisit GRPO ablation. All four corpora are matched on the same 200-report test split, with rates normalised by total word count.

Table 13: Stage 2 prompt — reasoning-trace SFT. The assistant target is a three-section report (<findings>, <thinking>, <impression>); inside <thinking>, uncertain regions are anchored via <objN> narrative tokens and inspected via detect() calls whose <region> coordinates are normalised to [0, 1]. Type-A samples (1,292/1,909) carry at least one revisit anchor; Type-B samples (617/1,909) have no detect() calls.

Table 12: Stage 1 prompt — uncertainty bounding-box detection (SFT). The assistant target is a JSON array (possibly empty) of bounding-box items. Coordinates are normalised to the [0, 223] image grid used by the Stage 1 visual head.
Table 5: Ablation study of UR2 on MIMIC-CXR (Best, Second-best). S1, S2, S3 denotes Stage1, Stage2, and Stage3, respectively. F1 here denotes CheXbert Macro F1.

Table 16: LLM-as-judge prompt used to score the <thinking> portion of generated reasoning traces. The judge is GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-11-20) called with temperature = 0 and JSON-mode output; identical seed is used across all reports to ensure reproducibility. For every test report and every model under evaluation, the prompt is instantiated by substituting the radiologist-written ground-truth report into {gt_report} and the model’s full <findings>/<thinking>/<impression> generation into {generated}. All five dimensions are scored on a 1–5 Likert scale; each score is accompanied by a one-sentence justification. Aggregate results are reported in Tab. 17.

Table 10: Stage 2 prompt for hedging rewrite with a self-correction fallback. Part (a) substitutes per-anchor variables for the original sentence, the matched ImaGenome scene-graph phrase, the anatomical region name, a unique narrative tag ⟨objn⟩, a stance label chosen from {confirm, qualify, alternative}, and a closed vocabulary of hedge terms (may, likely, could, appears, suggests, suggestive of, concerning for, consistent with, possible, probable, potential, perhaps). Part (b) reuses the same system content as (a). If both passes fail the verifier, a deterministic rule-based fallback inserts “may” or “which may” into the sentence; anchors whose rule-based output still fails are excluded from the SFT corpus.
